# bugs #2626: sdas ends with a segmentation fault for a macro call with more arguments than parameters

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2626/
- Category: [Already fixed in trunk](../../fixed-upstream.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as fixed in r11332. Consider a q error in place of the internal error for a macro call with too many arguments.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The crash does not occur on r17176. For the macro and the calls in the fourth comment, sdas8051 and
sdasstm8 print `?ASxxxx-Internal-fgetm(fp)-Error srcline` with a line number and return exit
status 3. The number is the line of the call whose string contains a comma.

The reporter found that the number of macro calls is not the cause. The call has more arguments
than the macro has parameters. `getxstr` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asmcro.c` ends an argument at a comma, a
space, or a tab, also between quotation marks, so `"seg,fault"` is two arguments. `macro` places an
`asmf` structure in `asmq` and then calls `qerr` because of the argument count. `qerr` returns to
`main` with `longjmp` before `macro` assigns `asmq->fp`, and `nxtline` passes the null pointer to
`fgetm`. A macro with one parameter, called with `2,3`, gives the same message. The two attached
files differ in one call, which has three arguments for a macro with two parameters.

`sdas/doc/asmlnk.txt` requires the form `^/ /` for a macro argument that contains a separator.
This form works on r17176 when the quotation marks are inside the delimiters. For
`stringtest ^/"seg,fault"/`, sdas8051 and sdasstm8 assemble the bytes of the string. A string with
a semicolon assembles in this form as well.

## Fixed by

[r11332](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/11332/), which applied the patch from the fifth
comment. Before r11332 `fgetm` dereferenced the null pointer. r11332 adds a check, and `fgetm`
ends the run with the message above.

## Related

For a macro call with too many arguments, the assembler still ends the run with a message about an
internal error. The `<q>` error that `macro` raises for the call is not printed, because the run
ends in the first pass. If `macro` assigned `asmq->fp` before it parses the arguments, the
assembler could print the `<q>` error and continue. This change was not tried.

The last comment refers to bug #3150 for the `^/ /` form. Bug #3150 concerns the delimiter of the
`.ascii` and `.str` directives, and it reproduces on r17176 with sdas8051. It does not affect
macro arguments.
